newsitem.title: CHILE: SOCCER-ZAMORANO SCORES TWICE AS CHILE BEAT PARAGUAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZAMORANO SCORES TWICE AS CHILE BEAT PARAGUAY.

text.p: Ivan Zamorano, who appears to be leading his country almost single-handedly toward next year's World Cup, scored both goals as Chile beat Paraguay 2-1 Sunday.
Zamorano took his tally in the World Cup qualifiers to twelve in as many games and kept Chile in fourth place in the South American group with 19 points, two ahead of fifth-placed Bolivia.

Paraguay's defeat, their second in a row, cost them the leadership of the group as they were overtaken by Argentina, but they are still well-placed to qualify. The top four teams will go to France next year.
Chile's Victor Hugo Castaneda and Paraguay goalscorer Hugo Brizuela were sent off for fighting in the second half as tempers flared in a fiercely-contested game, played before a 76,000 crowd.
Castaneda had made his mark in the ninth minute when he won the penalty from which Zamorano opened the scoring.
The goal ruined Paraguay's defensively-orientated tactics, forcing them to open up more than they had intended.
Zamorano struck again in the 51st minute when he rose between two defenders to head in a cross by Cristian Castaneda.
But Brizuela reduced the deficit ten minutes later when he pounced on a rebound in the penalty area, just one minute after coming on as a substitute.
Both teams missed good chances in a dramatic finale.
The win maintained Chile's 100 percent home record in the qualifiers and they have the bonus of playing three of their last four games at home.
Paraguay have lost two of the three games they have played without captain and first-choice goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert, who received a four-match suspension after being sent off against Colombia.

Chile - Nelson Tapia, Cristian Castaneda, Ronald Fuentes, Javier Margas, Miguel Ponce, Luis Musrri, Clarence Acuna (Fernando Cornejo, 81), Marcelo Vega (Esteban Valencia, 70) , Victor Hugo Castaneda, Ivan Zamorano, Marcelo Salas.

Paraguay - Danilo Aceval, Francisco Arce, Catalino Rivarola, Carlos Gamarra, Celso Ayala, Harles Bourdier, Estanislao Struway, Roberto Acuna, Julio Enciso, Aristides Rojas, (Jose Cardozo, 46), Richard Baez (Hugo Brizuela, 60).
